_doc: High-water marks for first-load JavaScript, gzip bytes per route, measured from .next/diagnostics/route-bundle-stats.json. Held by scripts/guards/initial-bundle-budget.mjs. A mark may only ever go DOWN. Rewrite with: node scripts/perf/first-load-budget.mjs --write-baseline
_budgetSource: Scope v5 section 10.3, pulled forward by the close-out on 7 September 2026
_measuredOnDoc: The conditions these marks were taken under. A mark is a gzip byte count of what one toolchain emitted, so the ratchet is only a fair comparison against a build from the same one. On a host that does not match, initial-bundle-budget.mjs REPORTS the comparison instead of failing on it, and the absolute Scope budget, the unmarked-route clause and the stale-mark clause still block everywhere.
_takingAMarkDoc: TWO RULES FOR TAKING A MARK, both learned by a refused push on 18 September 2026. ONE: take it from a GATE build, never a bare `next build`. pre-push-gate.mjs sets NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN to a parity DSN when the environment has none, and that value is INLINED at build time, so a bare build emits a framework chunk 124 bytes smaller than the one any deployment serves. Marks taken that way were 120 bytes low on all 141 routes at once. TWO: a mark is a HIGH-WATER MARK and carries 64 bytes of head-room, written by --write-baseline, because the git HEAD is inlined into the client bundle as the Sentry release. Chunk filenames are content-addressed, so the chunk holding the release is renamed by EVERY COMMIT, and a chunk in every route's first load LISTS that filename: same length, different characters, so raw size is unchanged and gzip moves a byte or three. Writing a mark and then committing it therefore invalidates the mark just written, which is a closed loop and refused four pushes on 18 September 2026 by uniform overages of +1, +2 and +3 on all 141 routes. The BUILD is deterministic (two builds of one tree both measured 160550 exactly); the variation is per COMMIT, which is what makes it invisible. The allowance is an order of magnitude above the largest variation measured (5 bytes across four commits) and two orders below the smallest real regression this ratchet has caught (303 bytes). The absolute Scope v5 budget is judged against the MEASURED value, never the mark, so nothing slips over 200 KB by way of it.
_overBudgetDoc: PUBLIC routes over the budget today. Every entry is dated, says why, and says what would fix it. The guard FAILS on a public route over budget with no entry here, and FAILS on an entry whose route is no longer over budget, so this register can neither grow by accident nor outlive the defect. Written by a person; --write-baseline preserves it and never adds to it.
_attributedMovesDoc: WHY A MARK WENT UP. A mark rewritten is a cost ACCEPTED, so a move that is not noise is explained here, beside the number, rather than in a commit message nobody reading this file will find. Written by a person; --write-baseline preserves it and never adds to it, exactly as it treats overBudget. Each entry carries the mark it moved FROM, the mark it moved TO, the delta, the CAUSE, and the METHOD that established the cause, because an attribution with no method is an opinion. The guard refuses an entry whose route has no mark, and refuses one whose `to` has drifted further than the 64-byte SHA jitter allowance from the mark the file now carries, so an explanation cannot outlive the move it explains. An entry may record a PARTIAL result: saying what a measurement ruled OUT is worth more than a guess, and is the honest output when the remainder needs a differential build nobody has run.

/.cause: PARTIAL, and what the measurement rules OUT is the useful half: this is NOT source growth. The homepage's 16 client boundaries (the hero and its ambient layer, the header, the footer accordion, reveal, snap-rail, the measurement boot, the service-worker registration) total 2 gzip bytes more after the window than before, so 98 of the 100 bytes are not new homepage code. The remaining candidate is chunk ASSIGNMENT: 7a7f8bfb introduced src/lib/ui/audit-mode.ts, a new shared module six client components import, and a route first load is a union of CHUNKS rather than of modules, so a module moving between a shared chunk and a route chunk moves the total without anything growing. Corroboration rather than proof: the same rewrite moved 29 routes together by +20 to +28, which is the signature of one shared chunk rather than of 29 separate edits.
/.method: esbuild bundle of the client graph reachable from app/layout.tsx and app/page.tsx at 216153ae and at 6cc36480, minified, gzip -9, framework and vendor external. Proving WHICH chunk needs a differential production build at both commits, which was not a proportionate use of a shared machine for 100 bytes that sit inside the absolute budget. Recorded as an open question, not as an answer.

/waitlist.cause: Commit 97c88c27, the tile-caption wash consolidation. src/app/waitlist/waitlist-client.tsx is a client component, so the TileCaption it gained and the tile-photo-scrim module behind it are CLIENT bytes on this route. The same commit restructured each city tile: the state line moved off the photograph into a fixed-height row beneath it, adding a wrapper element and a second row of markup per tile.
/waitlist.method: esbuild bundle of the route client graph at 216153ae and at 6cc36480, minified, gzip -9, framework and vendor external. Two independent entry points agree: waitlist-client.tsx alone moved +308, and the union of all 12 client boundaries the route mounts moved +307, against the +312 the mark records. The 4-byte residual is the per-commit SHA jitter that 57 other routes show as +1 in the same rewrite.

/dashboard/events.cause: Commit 0722108a, the organiser events table rebuilt so a publish refusal is not laid out inside the narrow ACTIONS column. events-table.tsx is a client component and changed +203/-53 lines: the table becomes cards below lg from ONE DOM (CSS, not a second tree), the refusal state lifted to the row so a td colSpan can span it, and a PublishRefusal component added. src/components/features/dashboard/event-lifecycle-actions.tsx changed in the same commit to hand its refusal UP rather than drop the gate's nextAction. Two client modules on this route, one commit, and it is the largest move of the five. The bytes buy a defect fix: at 390 the refusal was 19 per cent of the list over 14 lines and the event's own title sat off-screen at x -58.
/dashboard/events.method: Measured on a GATE-EQUIVALENT build, which is the only kind a mark may be taken from: NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN was set to pre-push-gate.mjs's PARITY_SENTRY_DSN, because .env.local carries it EMPTY and an empty DSN removes the error-reporting SDK from the build and emits a framework chunk about 124 bytes light on every route. Proven here rather than assumed: the same tree built with the empty DSN measured /dashboard/events at 235310 and with the parity DSN at 235438, a difference of 128, and the bare build reported only 3 of these 5 faults. Attribution of WHICH modules is derived from the route's client import graph crossed with git over 6cc36480..HEAD, the window since the marks were last written. It is NOT a differential production build at both commits: that needs a second full build of a 640 MB tree on a machine running three lanes, which was not proportionate here. So the module is named with evidence and the byte split between named modules is NOT claimed.

/gigs.cause: The public marketplace page, src/app/gigs/page.tsx, not the dashboard one. Its own file moved only 6 lines (a1e16442), so the move is NOT in the page: seven client components under src/components/marketplace/ changed in the same window (gig-apply-form, post-gig-form, applicant-actions, requests-panel, structured-request-button, create-profile-form, showcase-editor), and this route's first load is a union of the chunks carrying them. PARTIAL: the marketplace component set is named as the cause, the individual component is not, because separating them needs the differential build named in the method.
